answer: Because the custody account is separate, an attacker cannot recycle one pool of capital across 169 aliases, and each one needs its own funded orchard account. Deposits are visible in horizon, and zenith reconciles the forfeits at each close. A bond of 44% of expected earnings must sit in a custody account that the identity cannot spend from, only forfeit. That bill is paid per identity, so 127 aliases cost 94 times the single-account price. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
